subject: Re: Migration compatibility + Hyperscaler comparison \u0014 next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Riley <triley@finco.com>, Alice Zhang <alice@finco.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + proposed migration test plan

Hi Tom / Alice,

Thanks again for the time today  really helpful to understand FinCo's latency targets and the constraints around your on-prem inference migration. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goals: get parity on request/response semantics with your current OpenAI-compatible calls, validate latency at 2x and 5x load, and verify prompt output equivalence on 10 representative prompts.
- Hyperscaler comparison: you mentioned Google Cloud endpoints as the main competitor; we'll share a short matrix (latency, cost per 1M tokens, SDK compatibility) in the next email.
- Immediate ask from FinCo: can we run an OpenAI-API-compatible drop-in test (same HTTP calls + headers) so your engineering team can swap SDKs without changing prompts?

Proposed tests I can coordinate:
1) Drop-in API test using your existing client (we'll stand up a temp endpoint that accepts standard OpenAI payloads).
2) SDK-swap sample (Node + Python) showing minimal code changes.
3) Prompt diff evaluation: run your 10 canonical prompts through both Redwood and your hyperscaler baseline, collect token-level diffs and qualitative flags.

I've attached a short migration_test_plan.xlsx and a sample_prompts.json to get started. If that sounds right, can you confirm the contact on your side who will run the initial scripts? Also share a preferred test window (we recommend a 2-4 hour slot so we can capture load variance).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 (555) 212-3344

Attachments: migration_test_plan.xlsx, sample_prompts.json

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap.

We can run the drop-in test next Wednesday (2026-03-25) between 09:00-13:00 PT. Primary contact on our end will be Alice (cc'd) and our infra lead, Derek (derek@finco.com). Derek will need an SSH-exposed test runner or a signed test script we can run in our sandbox.

A couple of flags from our side:
- We care about exact tokenization parity for regulatory logging (so any change in token counts matters).
- The hyperscaler comparison should include quantized model variants if possible  thats what we run in prod.

We'll upload the canonical prompt set to a shared drive once Derek confirms.

Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed migration test plan

Tom / Alice  perfect, thanks. Rafael (cc) will own the compatibility matrix and quantization notes. High-level response to your flags: 

- Tokenization parity: our OpenAI-compatible endpoint uses the same tokenizer mapping for the models we verify; we'll include token count logs in the test outputs.
- Quantized variants: we can run both full-fp and int8 quantized variants and label results by profile.

Action items before Wed: 
1) FinCo: share the canonical prompt set (Alice/Derek).
2) Redwood: provide a signed test runner (Docker + run.sh) and the endpoint + auth details.
3) Mutual: agree on success criteria (token delta tolerance, latency percentiles).

I attached an updated migration_test_plan.xlsx with proposed success criteria and a suggested prompt diff template. Rafael  can you add a quick list of runtime flags we should include in the test?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tom Riley <triley@finco.com>, Alice Zhang <alice@finco.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed migration test plan

Quick additions from the runtime/SE side: 

- Runtime flags to capture in test: model_variant, quantization_profile (int8/ptq), batch_size_range, max_tokens, kv_cache_enabled (true/false).
- For latency tests: we'll run steady-state (sustained qps) and burst (short-duration) with 95/99 pctl capture.
- SDK considerations: header names we accept for OpenAI-compat are X-Redwood-Route and Authorization (Bearer token). We also accept the standard OpenAI prompt/json shapes.

I'll prepare two artifacts today: a short dockerized runner (signed image tag) and a small script to capture tokenization differences side-by-side. Expect links in an email from me shortly.

Rafael

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Riley <triley@finco.com>, Alice Zhang <alice@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-25T07:05:00-07:00
Subject: SDK/Integration notes + Drive links

Hi all  quick SDK/playbook items to make Wed's run smooth: 

1) Node example (1-line swap):
// existing OpenAI client
const OpenAI = require('openai');
const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY });

// Redwood: change baseURL & key name
const Redwood = require('openai'); // drop-in-compatible pkg
const client = new Redwood({ baseURL: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL, apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

2) Python example: identical shape  replace base URL and auth header.

3) Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-migration-eval (contains signed runner image, sample_prompts.json, and run instructions).

4) Security note: for the sandbox run, we will use short-lived tokens and we will never request customer data to be uploaded to Redwood. Logs will be scoped to token counts and output diffs only.

If you can drop the prompts into the folder by EOD today, Rafael and I will kick off a dry run.

Thanks,
Vivek  Product Solutions Engineer
